thread:
anya: Quick thought 44 can we tuck a compact heatmap into the p95 header and move sampling into the scrubber?
sam: sounds promising. worried about discoverability.
matt: made two quick mocks: inline thin-heatmap + mini stacked above scrubber. link: https://figma.com/s/compact-heatmap
anya: inline keeps cards tight; stacked gives room for presets. mobile favors inline.
leo: accessibility nit: touch target min 44px and visible focus outline. keyboard must work (tab + arrow).
aria: contrast: small greens lose AA; propose darker palette + 1px stroke for selected bucket.
katie: copy: use "Sampling rate" label. tooltip: "Percent of requests shown to reduce noise" or shorter?
sam: prefer shorter: "Reduce noise so latency patterns are clearer." show transient numeric while dragging (e.g., "10%").
matt: implementation notes: add mini-heatmap variant, aria-live for drag announcements: "Sampling set to 10 percent".
leo: keyboard behavior: arrows = 1%, shift+arrow = 10%, home/end jump presets. aria-live should announce larger deltas only.
aria: for SR avoid >50 focusables. expose single listbox to cycle buckets and read counts.
anya: agreed. sighted hover still shows counts. compact mode hides bucket labels.
katie: I'll update tooltip copy.
prod-bot: preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/compact-heatmap-preview (expires in 48h)
anya: cool 54 let's run a 5-min usability test after preview is live. thanks :thumbsup:
